title: Leading teams across organizations; social cohesion
blurb: Explain what makes project teams different, how to lead across organizational and cultural boundaries, and how to build social cohesion in remote and hybrid teams.
question: A project mixes in-house engineers with a partner firm's advisers, working partly remotely. Teamwork is weak and nobody is sure who decides what. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest?

teach.h: Project teams are temporary and mixed
teach.body: A project team is brought together for a limited time, often from several organizations: the business, users and suppliers. That needs a different style of leadership from an established team. A temporary leader may find authority harder to exercise, and it is not unusual for team members to be more senior than the project manager. In plain English: you lead through collaboration and trust, not through the org chart.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3

teach.h: Across organizations and cultures: clear boundaries
teach.body: When people come from different organizations and cultures, the book's advice is to set clear boundaries within which people can flex. Inside the boundaries, people use their own judgement; at the edges, they know to involve others. A delegation matrix is one way to do this, for example making clear what external advisers can decide and where they only advise. PRINCE2 7 calls the underlying skill cultural intelligence: relating and working across cultures.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.1, 7.4.3; PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3.1

teach.h: A delegation matrix sets the boundaries
head: Decision area
Delivery team
External advisers
Project manager
teach.caption: Illustrative example. The matrix makes decision authority transparent and reduces confusion (7.4.3).

teach.h: One person per role? Often not
teach.body: Ideally each required role would have its own person, but this is often impractical. Roles are commonly combined in one person or shared between people. What matters is that roles reflect people's capability, authority and availability, and that gaps are spotted and handled, for example by upskilling or shifting responsibilities to someone more suitable. Generic, copied role descriptions rarely work.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.2; PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3.2

teach.body: Whether teams work virtually, in person or hybrid, the way people work with each other needs careful thought, both to use their time well and to build social cohesion: the trust and relationships that let a group work as a team. Co-located teams build it naturally through informal moments. Remote and hybrid teams need deliberate activities, such as syncing co-location days for key people and teams and allowing time for less structured conversation online.

teach.h: Weak cohesion in a hybrid team: what helps?

root.label: Team is hybrid and teamwork is weak

children.label: Sync co-location days for key people

teach.caption: Book 4.3.3: mandating co-location is unlikely to build cohesion; deliberate, well-planned contact does.

teach.h: Delegation matrix versus team skill matrix

teach.body: Quayside Engineering is building a harbour crane control system with advisers from a partner firm abroad, and half the team works remotely. Project manager Lucia Ferrante finds the advisers are either waiting for permission or overruling the team. In the project kickoff workshop the team builds a delegation matrix: advisers decide on safety standards and advise on design detail. Lucia also syncs two co-location days per release for key people and keeps the first ten minutes of online calls unstructured.

teach.text: Unclear decision rights are solved by a delegation matrix, not a skill matrix (which shows skills and gaps). And weak cohesion in a hybrid team is not fixed by mandating co-location or tightening agendas: plan how people work together and add deliberate relationship-building time.

items: Project teams are temporary and mixed; members may be more senior than the PM.
Across organizations and cultures: set clear boundaries within which people can flex (4.3.1).
A delegation matrix makes decision authority clear, for example for external advisers.
One person per role is ideal but often impractical; roles get combined or shared (4.3.2).
Build social cohesion deliberately in remote and hybrid teams (4.3.3).
Sync co-location days for key people; allow unstructured time online.

summary: You can now explain why temporary project teams need a different leadership style, and how clear boundaries help people work across organizations and cultures. You can also say how to build social cohesion in remote and hybrid teams, and why mandating co-location is not the answer.

A.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile recommend for working successfully across organizations and cultures?
options: Require every partner to adopt one shared culture
Set clear boundaries within which people can flex
Have the project manager approve each decision
Assign each role to someone with agile experience
A.why: Book 4.3.1: working across cultures requires setting clear boundaries within which people can flex.

whyNot.0: Forcing one culture ignores the advice to give people room to flex inside clear limits.
whyNot.2: Centralizing every decision contradicts flexing within boundaries and self-management.
whyNot.3: Assigning only agile-experienced people is often impractical and does not set boundaries.

A.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile say about assigning a separate person to each role?
options: It is ideal but often impractical, so roles are combined or shared
It is a requirement before the project can be authorized by the board
It applies to the delivery roles but not to the governance roles
It is set by the agile coach at each stage boundary
A.why: Book 4.3.2: ideally organizations would assign individuals to each required role, but this is often impractical.

whyNot.1: Authorization does not depend on one person per role; combining roles is common.
whyNot.2: The point applies to roles generally, not just to delivery roles.
whyNot.3: Role allocation is part of the organization practice, not an agile coach decision at boundaries.

A.q: Which activity does PRINCE2 Agile suggest to build social cohesion when teams work remotely?
options: Requiring every member to work from one office
Running each online meeting strictly to a fixed agenda
Replacing calls with written status updates
Syncing co-location days for key people and teams
A.why: Book 4.3.3: remote or hybrid teams may need extra activities such as syncing co-location days for key people and teams, focused on key relationships.

whyNot.0: Mandating co-location is unlikely to build social cohesion.
whyNot.1: A strict agenda may be efficient, but cohesion grows from less structured conversation.
whyNot.2: Written updates reduce contact; they do not build relationships.

B.q: A partner firm's advisers are unsure which decisions they can make and which they should only advise on. Which tool BEST clarifies this?
options: Team skill matrix
Product backlog
Delegation matrix
Risk register
B.why: A delegation matrix makes responsibilities and decision-making authority transparent (7.4.3), one way to set clear boundaries within which people can flex (4.3.1).

whyNot.0: The team skill matrix shows skills and gaps, not decision authority.
whyNot.1: The product backlog holds a team's user stories.
whyNot.3: The risk register records risks, not who decides what.

B.q:
Which two statements about project teams are correct?
1. Temporary project teams often need a different leadership style from established teams.
2. Team members report to the project manager through their line management.
3. Social cohesion matters whether teams are virtual, in person or hybrid.
4. Remote teams build cohesion best through formal meetings with fixed agendas.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Temporary teams need a different style of leadership (PRINCE2 7 3.3), and social cohesion must be built whatever the working pattern (book 4.3.3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: project team members often keep their own line managers and may outrank the PM.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: line authority is not the basis of project leadership, and cohesion needs less structured time.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: less structured conversation helps build cohesion.

B.q: In a hybrid team, which is MOST likely to build social cohesion?
options: Allowing time for less structured conversation online
Requiring every member to attend the office every day
Keeping each online meeting strictly to its agenda
Setting individual targets for every team member
B.why: Book 4.3.3 suggests allowing time for less structured conversations online to build social cohesion.

whyNot.1: Mandating co-location is unlikely to build cohesion.
whyNot.2: Strict agendas keep meetings efficient but squeeze out relationship building.
whyNot.3: Individual targets can pull people apart rather than build a team.

C.q: Which artifact helps set clear boundaries within which people can flex, and in which workshop is a team version created?
options: Team skill matrix, in the project kickoff workshop
Delegation matrix, in the project closure workshop
Agilometer, in the project initiation workshop
Delegation matrix, in the project kickoff workshop
C.why: A delegation matrix makes decision authority transparent (7.4.3), and the team delegation matrix is a topic of the project kickoff workshop (Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: The right workshop, but the skill matrix maps skills, not decision boundaries.
whyNot.1: The right artifact, but it is created at kickoff, not at closure.
whyNot.2: The Agilometer assesses how suitable the environment is for agile; it does not set decision rights.

C.q: Why can leading a project team be harder than leading an established team?
options: Project teams sit outside any governance structure
It is temporary and members may outrank the leader
Project teams are not permitted to self-manage
The project manager holds line authority over all
C.why: Temporary leaders may find authority harder to exercise, and team members may be more senior than the project manager (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Project teams work within governance set by the project board.
whyNot.2: Self-management is encouraged in PRINCE2 Agile within clear boundaries.
whyNot.3: The project manager usually lacks line authority, which is part of the difficulty.

C.q: A project manager proposes making office attendance compulsory to fix weak teamwork in a hybrid team. Which assessment is BEST?
options: Sound: co-location is required for agile teams
Sound: it gives the PM line authority over the team
Weak: plan deliberate contact to build cohesion
Weak: hybrid teams should switch to fully remote
C.why: Mandating co-location is unlikely to build social cohesion; the book suggests careful planning of how people work together, such as synced co-location days and unstructured time online (4.3.3).

whyNot.0: Co-location helps teamwork but is not required, and mandating it is unlikely to work.
whyNot.1: Office attendance does not create line authority, and authority is not what builds cohesion.
whyNot.3: Going fully remote is not the book's advice; deliberate cohesion-building is.

reteach.title: A wedding band of strangers
reteach.question: How do musicians who have never met play a great wedding set together on one day's notice?

blocks.h: Agree the frame, then trust each other
blocks.body: A band booked for one wedding agrees the set list, the key and who leads each song. Inside that frame, each player improvises freely. They arrive early to chat and run a few songs together, because a little time spent getting to know each other makes the whole evening better. Projects work the same way: clear boundaries, freedom inside them, and deliberate time to build relationships.

blocks.text: Forcing everyone into one room every day is not the same as building a team. Plan the contact that matters.

explain.body: Project teams are temporary and drawn from several organizations. Leaders earn authority through collaboration, and team members may be more senior than the project manager.

test.q: In a project team, it is not unusual for:
options: the PM to hold line authority over all members
team members to be more senior than the PM
the board to manage each developer directly
teams to work without any governance
test.why: It is not unusual for team members to be more senior than the project manager (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: The PM usually lacks line authority over project team members.
whyNot.2: The board directs; it does not manage developers day to day.
whyNot.3: Teams work within governance set by the board.

explain.body: Working across organizations and cultures needs clear boundaries within which people can flex. A delegation matrix can show what external advisers decide and where they advise.

test.q: Setting clear boundaries within which people can flex helps a project to:
options: work across organizations and cultures
remove the need for a project board
avoid agreeing separate management approaches
fix the scope of every release
test.why: Book 4.3.1: successfully working across cultures requires setting clear boundaries within which people can flex.

whyNot.1: The project board still directs the project.
whyNot.2: Management approaches are still agreed in initiation.
whyNot.3: Scope flexes in PRINCE2 Agile; boundaries are about decision freedom.

explain.body: Ideally each role has its own person, but this is often impractical, so roles are combined or shared. Match roles to capability, authority and availability.

test.q: When it is impractical to give each role its own person, PRINCE2 Agile accepts that roles are:
options: left empty until staff are found
transferred to the supplier
removed from the role descriptions
combined or shared between people
test.why: Book 4.3.2: assigning individuals to each role is often impractical, so roles are combined or shared.

whyNot.0: Leaving roles empty would leave responsibilities uncovered.
whyNot.1: Roles are not handed to the supplier by default.
whyNot.2: Role descriptions still describe every role, combined or not.

explain.body: Remote and hybrid teams need deliberate activities to build social cohesion, such as synced co-location days for key people and less structured time online.

test.q: Which BEST builds social cohesion in a remote team?
options: Weekly written status updates
Mandatory daily office attendance
Syncing co-location days for key people
Shorter online meetings with no informal chat
test.why: Book 4.3.3: syncing co-location days for key people and teams, focused on key relationships, builds social cohesion.

whyNot.0: Written updates share information but do not build relationships.
whyNot.1: Mandating co-location is unlikely to build cohesion.
whyNot.3: Cutting informal chat removes the less structured time that builds cohesion.
